name: comp-409

frames.best_why: All four portraits and the +3 circle are fully in view with no cursor over them.

tagline: Four faces overlap in a line and end in a dark +3 circle.
summary: A row of four circular portraits overlapping with dark rims, finished by a round grey button reading +3 for the people left out.
appearance: Four square portraits cropped to circles about 40px across overlap by a quarter of their width, each ringed in dark so the edges read. They end in a slightly larger charcoal circle holding a muted +3 that brightens to white on hover.
behaviour: Hovering the +3 circle lifts its text from grey to near white while the faces stay still; nothing opens or moves. The rest is static.
demo_content: Four stock portraits of women and the label +3.
search_phrases: who is in this group indicator
team members shown in a line
use_when: Showing a handful of people on a project or thread when the full list runs longer.
avoid_when: When every person must be reachable: the +3 control has no click action to reveal the rest.
customise: Portrait sources, their alt text and the +3 label are fixed in the file; showing real people means editing the image list and the button text.
weight_why: Four small images and one button; no script, no animation loop.

a11y.note: Portraits carry alt text, but the +3 button's label does not tell screen readers what the count stands for.

issues: The +3 button has no click handler, so it hints at more people but opens nothing.
polish_why: Even overlap and spacing, but the +3 control is a plain grey circle that leads nowhere.
